- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and model forecasts rise, it often overcorrects; apply downward bias of 2–5% to avoid overbought bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average of true values.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.  
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >5% per week), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 2–3 periods.  
- If sentiment is uniformly high and model forecast is flat, it often underestimates; apply upward bias of 2–4% to avoid complacency.
